I also showed the judge the village when we were on the -- when we were doing the on-site village. There were even some villagers there who confirmed that we had not mistreated them. I accounted for my statement to the police by saying that I simply wanted to cut their manhandling short, and that that was why I said what I said in the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'd like to offer into evidence 65 ter 1D2725.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I would raise the same concern I did for the previous Official Note, which I believe that the Chamber admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, this is a statement given by this witness. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1543.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, understanding that you take issue with some of these items, sir, that -- did you in fact tell the police that you had met Zec, Petric, and Patak at an inn called the Centaur [phoen] in late August before you went to Gosici. Putting aside whether or not it is true, did you tell the police that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you tell the police that before you left Vodice, your village, that you put on camouflage uniforms?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: At times we would assemble in Vodice and then go to -- to the field in Zrmanja. I told you that I would make certain statements that had nothing to do with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And I'm asking you what you told the police, sir. I understand that you take issue. I'm just asking that you told the police these things. So we understand each other, exactly where my questions are coming from you. Did you tell the police that after you got to Gosici that Petric went into a house, and after he left the house, the house was shortly on fire. Did you tell the police that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I never mentioned Gosici. I talked about the village to which I subsequently took the investigating judge to see. There was a confusion in my head, and I said things that had nothing to do with the truth. I told them that I was in that particular village with Petric, and no houses were on fire, nobody came to any harm. It was the police who wrote down Gosici, and I signed the statement without reading it. I talked about a different village, where there was no shooting going on. I -- I talked about the village that I referred to in my earlier answer. It's a village beyond Ervenik, the village that I took the investigating judge to see. I didn't mention Gosici at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, on the village that you were talking about, did Petric go into a house and put the house on fire, or you noticed the house was on fire after he left?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. We got there, went into the house, searched the place a bit, and left. There were pigs about. We took a couple of pigs into our car and left. I talked about the house, about the appearance of the door, the colour of the door, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, sir, with regard to this incident in Gosici, were you aware that Mr. Petric gave a statement to the police about this incident?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: He did mention it, but he also said that he mentioned it on account of the mistreatment he was accorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And with regard to the events in Gosici, you were in fact charged with those -- with crimes from Gosici, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was a suspect in the case of the killing of Serb civilians in Gosici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, during the course of -- of interviews with Mr. Petric, did you become aware that Mr. Petric said that you and he stole sheep and sold them to an individual by the name of Branko?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: He was a butcher from the general area of Vodice. He bought the sheep.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: As we were on our way back from the field, we would see sheep milling freely about, and we'd take some, because Petric had been told by this butcher to bring them some sheep, if he came across any.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm referring for is 1D -- 65 ter 1D2747, Mr. Petric's statement of 16 October 1995, Counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now the sheep that you and Mr. Petric took, did you sell it to Branko?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you split the money?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you ever find out who these sheep belonged to?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: To put it simply, this was abandoned livestock, wondering freely about. There were sheep, cows, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Did you come to learn that Petric told the police that you and Petric went to Gosici looking for this forester? Did you know that Petric told the police that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I did hear about him telling certain things to the police, but he told them things because they mistreated him. But he was referring to the calf that belonged to that old man, whereas they kept referring to the forester. I know that Petric, just like me, told them things that had nothing to do with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, we'll offer 65 ter 1D2747, consistent with Your Honours' other rulings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Same position, Your Honour. I think it's another statement of [indiscernible] -- of a witness on the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. To be MFI'd, and 25 words to be added to the submissions. Could I ask some clarifying questions, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, you told us that you never mentioned Gosici, that you were confused at the time, and that, actually, you talked about a village beyond Ervenik, the village that you took the investigating judge to see. Now, you were then asked whether you saw Petric in that village go into a house and put the house on fire, and you said, No, we got there, and you went into the house and searched the place, although this is misspelled in the transcript, a bit and then you left. Was there, in that house, was there someone still living in that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There were civilians in the village, about a dozen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In that house as well? The house -- or did you go through all the houses in that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We did not. We only entered that house, and there were people living in it. And we also saw some other civilians living there as we passed by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you said there were pigs, and you took a couple of pigs. Those pigs were at that house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were around milling about the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So you're saying, these pigs, did they belong to these villagers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, they did. The civilians there even helped us catch the two pigs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did they give you permission to take these pigs or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We asked them, and they said it was okay. They helped us catch them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then they gave them as a gift to you, under those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No one threatened them or anything. This was all done in a friendly manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you sold them as well as the lambs or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you do with the pigs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We split them between ourselves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you -- for consumption?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: They didn't ask for any compensation for the pigs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can I just ask a couple of follow-up questions from your inquiry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, when you were getting these pigs, you were walking in this village with Mr. Petric, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When we were in Kistanje, when we took it up, we saw there was a lot of firewood in a house. Then Petric asked that we come back with a van, which I had, to have the firewood taken to his house in Vodice. We did so, and on our way we entered the village where the people were, and that's where we got the two pigs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And when you got these two pigs, you were armed, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: One always moves about with a weapon. It was still in the period when you could have Serb stragglers in the villages, soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now, going back to Mr. Petric and Mr. Petric's statement, and I'm referring to 1D2726 at this point, did you come to learn, Mr. Perkovic, that Mr. Petric told the police that both you and he had set fire to the forester's house in Gosici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: The police brought me to see Petric to confront him. They asked him that question, and then he winked at me and responded, Yes. But he had obviously been treated and beaten by the police. They confronted us. I was interrogated in one room and he in another, and then he said that we were in Gosici. Then I told them that we had nothing to do with Gosici and that we never went there, that this had to do with Zrmanja and the calf promised by that man. I think they got some things mixed up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time we'll to offer into evidence 65 ter 1D2726, consistent with Your Honours' rulings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's another one of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's another one of the MFI'd 25 additional words for the submissions. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, in addition to this document, the last document didn't receive a number. That was 1D2747. That will become Exhibit D1544, marked for identification. The current document is 1D2726, and that will receive Exhibit D1545, also marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I add something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes, the first one, then, was 1D2747, which now received D1544, yes, I just wanted to check that, as always, Mr. Registrar had been very accurate. Both the 1544 and D1545 are marked for identification. You would like to add something, Mr. Perkovic. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When we were confronted, Petric and I, during the interrogation at the police station, the police brought me in the room where Petric had been, and then they asked Petric, Tell us if you were in Gosici. He winked at me and he said, yes, and then I jumped and said, Petric, what you are talking about? We never went to Gosici in our lives. And then the police also came -- some additional police came to the interrogation room, and then they started beating us, mistreating us, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this addition. Please proceed, Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Turning our attention to 65 ter 1D2729, Mr. Perkovic, were you aware that Mr. Ladovic, Patak gave a statement concerning your participation in Gosici to the police? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Patak is a drunkard. He is simply silly. And he said things to the police much the way I did on occasions. He was also mistreated by the police, interrogated for the same amount of time, and no wonder he told them all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, staying with that, were you aware that he told the police that you and Petric and he and others met at the cafe in Vodice before you went on to Gosici? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Sometimes from Vodice, we went in the field to Zrmanja, but no Gosici were involved. I didn't know about Gosici itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, staying with Mr. Ladovic, were you aware that he told the police that it was in fact your idea to go to Gosici that day?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And likewise, were you aware that he told the police that you and Petric had set fire to a house in Gosici? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, subject to Your Honours' other prior rulings on this score, we offer into evidence 65 ter 1D2729.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which will be marked for identification, Mr. Hedaraly. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D1546, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And will keep that status for the time being. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Going back to your actual trial, sir, you were in fact tried for the events in Gosici, were you not?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And it went through the court system up to the higher courts, did it not?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: First, there was a proceedings after which I was imprisoned for nine months. Then I was acquitted. And then the prosecutor appealed the court decision, and the proceedings were returned to the Sibenik court because that area fell under the Sibenik county. Therefore, the case was heard before the Sibenik court. Finally, as the proceedings developed, the prosecutor dropped charges, although it was coming to its close. We -- witnesses were heard but ultimately the Prosecutor, Mr. Zganjer dropped charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I might have one moment. I do believe I'm near conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: One last question, Mr. Perkovic, concerning Varivode. Were you ever accused of the killings that took place in Varivode?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I do believe I got in under the wire time-wise, and I appreciate it, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you did, Mr. Kehoe. Any questions for the witness, Mr. Cayley?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Nothing from us, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: No questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, I take it there's a need to cross-examine the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it already possible to give us any indication time-wise? It is a viva voce witness, that is different from 92 ter witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There is still a lot of ground to cover under 90(H), but I will try to finish today, Mr. President. I don't want to offer that as a guarantee at this time, but I will definitely try to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may, just by pure convenience, if counsel is not going to complete today, we had a witness waiting, so if I can just can tell VWS to take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I do understand that you certainly -- if you will be able to finish today that not much time will be left, which makes it a wise thing to do, is to start for five or seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. That being said, perhaps it will be cut short depending on the examination. But that is it my estimate at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I suggest that we -- we wait until the next break and then get a further indication and if there's no chance that the next witness will start today, you will then know that in approximately 30 to 45 minutes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Perkovic.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I am counsel for the Prosecution in this case, and I just want to ask you some questions about, first of all, the Gosici incident for which you were tried and on some other matters. If at any time any of my questions are unclear, please feel free to ask me to rephrase so that can I clear up any misunderstanding. First of all, you mentioned you were interviewed by the police on 16 and 17 October; right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it is that date, but, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let's look quickly at D1539, which is the Official Note of the interview you were shown -- about the first interview you had with the police. And can you, while the document comes up, can you tell us did that interview take place on the same date that you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: The interview that the police will with me was at the time when I was brought in. That was in the 36 hours, the day and night, at that time. All interrogation was during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So if the date on the note of 16 October is accurate, that means you would have been arrested either on the 16th or shortly beforehand; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to the last page -- actually, the last paragraph of this Official Note of 16 October.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And will you see a reference in the last paragraph: "Asked whether he heard about what had happened in Varivode and Gosic. He stated several times that he heard that ten civilians had been killed in Varivode, but he personally has never been to neither Gosic nor in Varivode." Do you remember saying that to the police officers?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I told them that I heard of some Serb civilians being killed in Gosici. I went there once with a van, and I was stopped by the police at a check-point. They told me I had to wait. I asked what it was all about and they told me that some Serbs had been killed in the village of Gosici. I had no knowledge of Varivode.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you stated there and you stated several times today already you had never in fact been to Gosici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Even to the present day, I don't know where they are. I was taken somewhere by the judge and the police, but I couldn't see where we were going. We arrived at this place and the judge saw that, basically, there had nothing to do with what I was telling him about. There were no higher buildings there, just ground-floor houses. We were even taken to Varivode.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. That's on the 16th of October. On the next day you were interviewed again, and that was also referenced today. That's D1543.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we can go to the bottom of page 1 in English and the last paragraph in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when that note comes up on the screen, you will see a there's a sentence at the bottom where -- in the police note, the police writes down that you went to a village he thinks is Gosici. So a village you thought was Gosici. So is that something that you told the police, that you went to a village you thought was Gosici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I have been talking about that village in Ervenik all the time. But at the time I didn't think much about what I was saying because I so physically and psychologically abused that I signed anything. And what I told them I repeated before the investigating judge. He had pictures of the village of Gosici and he could conclude for himself that what I was talking about had nothing to do with the truth. Admittedly, that was not his intention, though, because he just needed someone to put away. The pressure was so great at the time to discover the perpetrators that they had to do something. There were threats levelled stating that you will be sent to The Hague and Croatia will not be admitted into the EU. They did what they had to. We were physically and psychologically mistreated by the police. He was the one who beat me the most, this Markovic guy and a colleague of his. They just wanted to force an admission from us and to tell us that we were in Gosici. They just wanted to have us displayed as perpetrators. The police were not doing their jobs properly. And the courts were not going about it properly as well. So many years have passed by and it is still unknown who the perpetrators of the murders in Gosici and Varivode is. And I ask you what is the reason for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, sometimes I will pause just to have the full answer interpreted. We'll get into some of these matters in more detail. You don't have to give all your answer in one shot. I will ask you specific questions. If there is anything that you want to add that I have not covered, the Presiding Judge will give you an opportunity to do so. But let's try to focus on the question so we can go through this methodically, and we'll talk about the other aspects that you have mentioned. Is that okay with you? If we can go to 65 ter 7308. Now, on that same day, where you said you were mistreated by the police, you were also taken to an investigating judge, to give a statement to the investigating judge. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: After 36 hours, they took me to see an investigative judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we go to page 3 of the English and page 3 of the B/C/S -- and just for the Court's reference, there are some handwritten notes on these documents. There is some highlighting. This is how we obtained them pursuant to a Request for Assistance from the Croatian government, so we don't know who made those markings, just so that it's clear it wasn't the Prosecution in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, do you see a handwritten note on the right saying "no upper floor"?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know where that is. I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can move to the right of the -- in B/C/S. It says in B/C/S "nema kata."

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I see it, no upper floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we go to the next page, returning to the issue of the village of Gosici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The next page in English, page 5; page 4 in the B/C/S, the next-to-last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You apparently said to the investigative judge: "I would like to check if that is it indeed that particular village, because I am accused of killing some old lady, and I know I did not do it." Do you remember saying that to the investigative judge?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. "I never spoke to the investigative judge ... I always said that when we were on the upper floor of the house that no one was killed there." I was talking about a village in Ervenik. This is the way I pictured it in my head.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: As for what it says, no upper floor, I don't know what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we can have 65 ter 7308, the record of the interview with the investigating judge, tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Can we have MFI, so I can just take a look at it at the break. And then I will just get back and see -- see just looking at the entire document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be MFI'd for the time being. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2556, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could I ask one clarifying question. Mr. Perkovic, you said that you were threatened that you would be sent to The Hague and that Croatia would not be admitted into the EU. Who said that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The police. Alongside the beating, they used a bat to hit me with. They also brought me a paper stating that I was discharged from the Croatian military. As of day one, in 1991, I was fighting for Croatia, and what fate do I meet in the end? I was simply brushed aside. I was beside myself. I could not believe such things were happening to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Did the investigating judge also put to you that it was -- that the discovery of the perpetrators was important for admission of Croatia into the European Union?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He didn't say that to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it was just the police. Was it one police officer or several police officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Several of them who interrogated me. There were three or four of them at one point, and all of them were questioning me and beating me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And all of them told you that it was important to -- whether true or not, to find some perpetrators in order for Croatia to have a better chance to be admitted to the EU?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They said, It is because of you that we will not be admitted. Because of you who had committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If I would tell you that the application for membership of the EU came years and years after the month of August 1995 -- month of October 1995, do you have any explanation as why they said that it was because of you that Croatia would not be admitted? Whereas there was no application --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. That's what the policeman said, You are going to The Hague, and Croatia will not be admitted to the European union because of you who committed crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You had another interview with the investigative judge roughly ten days later. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we could have 65 ter 7309 in the meantime on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, you remember meeting the investigative judge on 27 October 1995?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: It was the following day, one day after they placed me in detention that I asked to be able to steak to, I think it was the president of the court, and I told the man that I had never been to Gosici and had nothing to do with the murders. That's why I went over there, to tell him that, and nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you a record of an interview that you gave to the investigative judge ten days after your first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And if we go to the bottom in the English and top of page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And it reports that you told him, When you asked me before about Gosic, I told you something; however, I can say now that I don't remember that we have ever been to Gosic. I don't even know which village that would be [sic]. When I talked to you, I was still under the impression of what I've heard in the police, where they questioned me for a long time."

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And then if we go to the next page in English at the bottom, the same page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You say again: "Everything I told you on 17 October, I told you under the impression of what I've heard in the police." And my question for you is: Do you remember, after giving your first statement to the judge, giving them a second statement, where you indicated that what you said in your first interview was not correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. I met him only once, and I told him that what I said to the investigating judge had been said under the impression of what had been going on when I was being interrogated by the police. So that's what I told the judge at the time. But it was only once more that I met with the investigating judge at my request.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can tender 65 ter 7309, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Same as before, Your Honour. If we could just MFI it, just take a look at it at the break, appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, it will be MFI'd for the time being. Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2557, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And finally, you recalled later that in fact you were in Knin the day before the murders in Gosici, and you were in Cista Vglika the day after; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. When I was in prison, I saw that I was charged with the murder of the Serb civilians in Gosici. In the calendar I saw that on the 25th of August, the freedom train was running. That was the same date when I was charged with these murders. On that day I was wearing civilian clothes and was with my friends aboard the freedom train. In other words, I was not on duty in the army. I was off duty in civilian clothes. I was in Cista Vglika, that's a village that was occupied where we had a plot land. I went to Cista Vglika with my father in order to have our property that was there evaluated for damage by a damage assessor. I had eye-witnesses who saw me aboard the freedom train. There was a soldier. There was a name -- a man by the name of Cipal, which the general here might know. Unfortunately, he didn't remember seeing me. But there was another soldier who was in civilian clothes at the time who remembered seeing me aboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you part of the judgement in your case, which is at P1076, and if can I start with page 9 of the second translation in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: There are two translations uploaded. So page 9 of the second translation, which would be page 22 of the original B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And there's a reference there where it says that -- the judge is talking about you and saying: "Of course, he was trying to remember where he was on the day in question on August 27 ... after he was detained. And he could determine that in relation to the previous day, August 26th, because he was in Knin waiting for the liberty train to arrive. He was seen by Zivko Mato, Antonio, and Ante Roca [phoen] from Vodice. A day after Knin and the liberty train, so immediately after the day in question he was in Cista Velika, his father's village with his father Ante and his aunt." Is that consistent with your recollection of where you were on those days?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And just for the record, I don't need to go through it. There's another reference to where he was at page 79 of the English judgement, page 73 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I want to briefly mention the mistreatment that you talked about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to page 71 of the English, page 67 of the B/C/S of that judgement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And there's a general statement here about all of the accused in that case, some of which were mentioned today. Actually, can you name for us who else was accused with you of the murders of Gosici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Ivica Petric; Nikola Rasic, aka, Zec; I, and who was the fourth one? Patak Ladovic. I'm not sure if it was him. I don't remember anymore. There were four of us who were charged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. And it says there: "The accused, who gave different statements during the investigation, are explaining the reasons for it, and particularly explaining that their defence is result of mental and physical pressure and mistreatment in the police station which forces the court to analyse not only numerous evidence but the parts where the truthfulness of the evidence of the defence of the accused could not be controlled." And it goes on. Now, you described briefly for us the mistreatment that you were subject to. During the trial or any other time, did you hear that the other accused in your case had also been mistreated by the police?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I heard stories, and in the course of the interrogation itself, I heard moans from the beatings. I heard, in other words, them being beaten in the neighbouring rooms, and I also heard them say so in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I think you described for us how you were mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: In the interest the time, Mr. President, I won't go into the details, but it can be found on page 84 of the judgement in English, the portion where the judge in that case discusses the claims of mistreatment by Mr. Perkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you now, Mr. Perkovic, that is on the record, so I'm not going to ask about the mistreatment. But it is -- you have testified to it, and it is the judgement itself, just so you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to page 96 of the English judgement, and page 85 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It says -- it's the top paragraph in the B/C/S, the first full paragraph in the English: "In the course of investigation, eye-witness Dusan Borak and Bozo Borak were asked to recognise the accused in a line up of men, among them who were accused Perkovic, Ladovic, Rasic, and Petric. Both witnesses agreed and were convinced that among the men in the lineup, they did not recognise any of the men they had seen in Gosic on the day of the crime, while witness Dusan Borak said to be certain that none of the men in the lineup had been there." Do you remember being part of such a lineup?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, while I was in detention in Zadar, we were sent for the identification parade, and they invited the Serb civilians. I think that during the trial in Zadar, there were eye-witnesses who confirmed that they had never seen us, so I'm not referring to the situation which took place in the prison, but, rather, to what happened in the courtroom itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you -- did you know, or did you ever read that judgement of the -- of the trial court in Zadar which acquitted you of the crimes in Gosici?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: That's a pile of paper, I didn't even read that through. I know the way the trial proceeded, and I suppose the minutes merely reflect that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you remember if -- were any reasons given to you as to why you were being acquitted of those crimes?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the first trial or the second? There were two in Zadar and ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: The first one, the one in Zadar.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: We were acquitted in respect of Gosici and Varivode. It was said there was no evidence that we had perpetrated these offences and for -- and as for the other suspects in respect of other crimes, they were convicted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were you aware -- were you told by the judge in Zadar or anyone else that the reason you were acquitted was because the -- the statement you gave to the police and the investigative judge was unreliable and inconsistent with other evidence?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Rather, he was able to see that for himself, once he attended the scene and the reconstruction of the events. He was able to satisfy himself that we were not the perpetrators. He didn't comment on the statement taken by the police, although we had told him that he had been mistreated.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I just move on, Mr. President. The judgement is in evidence and has -- has all the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, about the second -- the second trial in Sibenik, you said that the state attorney's office abandoned prosecution. Were you ever told why?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: They didn't say anything but the papers did. I have a newspaper article with me in the hotel which says that for four, six years people who had not committed crimes were being tried, while there was evidence indicating that other perpetrators existed. This isn't something that the prosecutor himself stated. This was the papers. Even the judge in Zadar made a statement, which I have a copy of in the hotel, that it was not the actual perpetrators who were being tried in Sibenik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you show these newspapers articles to the members of the Defence when you talked to them yesterday?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't know if the Chamber is interested in those -- in those newspaper articles that the witness has at his hotel. I don't think it is critical in light of the evidence, but I leave it in the Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kehoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I'm sure counsel can get them on a wire service. They were public newspaper articles regarding these events. Which -- the wire service articles that the Office of the Prosecutor gets on a daily basis, so I'm sure they can get these. I don't have them. I never took anything from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we haven't seen those newspaper articles, and I do not know exactly from what date they are. It might not be easy to retrieve them. Would you mind to give a copy to Mr. Hedaraly of those newspaper articles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have all the newspapers on me. The journalists wrote these articles at the time of these trials, 1995, 1996, or 1997. For as long as three trials lasted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, again it is up to you if you are interested to --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I mean I would be interested --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... for the Chamber, then ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I mean, maybe the best way is if we get a copy, we can make a selection if we deem anything is -- could assist the Chamber in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The witness refers to what was written at the time about the event. Would you mind if through the intervention of the Victims and Witness Section that you would give the relevant newspapers to us so that they can be copied and that you get the originals returned to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you also assist us to find in those newspapers where exactly the relevant articles are found.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have complete newspapers. These are article clippings. I cut out the relevant articles, indicating that there are other suspects, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Registrar, could you inform the Victims and Witness Section that they assist in receiving from the witness the newspaper clippings, and that they will be copied, and the originals to be returned to him. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If I can have 65 ter 7310 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you mentioned you were never given a reason by the prosecutor why it was dropped. Let me show you the statement of reasons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Go to the statement of reasons as to why the indictment against you was dropped in Sibenik. Go to the second page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It says many things. The portion I'm interested in is in the middle of English. It says: "Namely, the heard witnesses who resided in Gosic and Varivode at the time of perpetration of the crimes indicated a completely different, bigger number of the perpetrators and a completely different way of perpetration of the crimes ..." And there's some more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just move to the next page of the English, the last paragraph of the text.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It says: "Since these first statements of the accused, which I reiterate by their content objectively, were never an unexplicit, unequivocal, and complete confession of the crimes, were completely eliminated as true and reliable during the repeated procedure of the trial before the court. So with the lack of any other facts and evidence, that would be the ground for establishment of the criminal responsibility of the accused for the mentioned crimes, the quoted indictments should be dropped." Mr. Perkovic, is that consistent with your understanding as to why the indictment against you was dropped by the Sibenik court?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I was able to see that the witnesses themselves testified that there was a larger group of individuals involved. I understood this to have been the reason why the charges were dropped. They heard these difference statements and concluded that we were not the perpetrators.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. President, if could I tender 65 ter 7310 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: No objection, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit P2558.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, to your knowledge, is it -- has the investigation into the crime -- the murders in Gosici and Varivode, have they been solved to this day?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. Nobody has been convicted for that, and nobody knows who committed the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And now you stated earlier that -- in your testimony a little earlier when you gave that long response and then the Judge asked you some follow-up questions, that, essentially, and I'm paraphrasing you, I don't believe that's correct, that in your opinion the police were not interested in -- in finding the perpetrators, but just to charge someone. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: The police didn't do their job properly. They didn't conduct a reconstruction on the scene of the crime. They didn't find bullet casings, et cetera. Evidently, since they didn't go about doing it, they didn't feel it was in their interest to do so. It was only on the basis of the statements that were forced out of us and on the basis of what we said in the courtroom that they were trying to have us convicted, rather than on the basis of the evidence that existed on the ground. The pace of it all was a very accelerated one. I'm referring to Gosici and Varivode, not to the other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you mentioned earlier today in your answers, in one of your first answers to my questions, that they were under a lot of pressure to process someone. Can you tell us what -- do you know what was the basis of that pressure?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: In my opinion, they wanted to find the perpetrators and to have the perpetrators processed. I know that there were quite a few soldiers who were in detention with me who were brought to justice. So the general tendency was to have all the perpetrators of crimes punished. It's just that it was not done in respect of Gosici and Varivode. I know that, in general, soldiers were being punished for the crimes they did. Why it was not done in this case, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And when you were saying they were being punished for the crimes they did, what crimes -- what type of crimes are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Individual cases of murders of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And do you know any -- any -- any specific examples of people being punished for murders of civilians?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, we just heard about them. Ivica Petric; the individual, Lasan from Vodice; Mario Dukic, who was with me in the prison; Zec, who was convicted for wounding the old lady; then there was another one who was commander of mine during the war. Apparently there was an old woman who was about to throw a hand-grenade, and he killed her, and he is just now serving his six-year sentence. The trial went on for quite a while. So I know of several such cases where people were tried and convicted. There was even mention of a village just above Sibenik. Some people were suspects in the murder of certain elderly people. The first accused in that case absconded. He left Croatia. This is the case involving the place called Prukljan, where an old man and woman were killed. The other co-accused in the case are still being tried. There were four of them. Three are in are in the prison, whereas one of them, who was the first accused, absconded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Misetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, just two issues. I believe in page 76, line 10, the witness described the ethnicity -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have page 76, line 10, I have a question. So I have some --

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: I'm -- apparently the numbering is off in the LiveNote on the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I will have a look at it. One second.

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: It's line 11 on the LiveNote on the main system, but there is one line off on the system on my computer, so it's line 10 in my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was part of the answer as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. MISETIC
utterances.text: Yes. And then there is a second issue, which is I'm told there was the name of one additional perpetrator that was missed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The first, I think -- Murders of civilians, did you refer to Serb civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mentioned quite a number of persons that were put to justice. You mentioned Ivica Petric, Zec. And did you mention another person in this context?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The little guy called Lasan or Laso and Sunjerga, Zeljko Sunjerga, who is serving his sentence right now. He was convicted in respect of an old woman. And he is serving a six-year sentence. Apparently she had a hand-grenade under her dress, and was about to throw it to him. At any rate, he was sentenced to six years of imprisonment. Then is there a Mario Dukic, I mentioned him as well. He was with me in the detention, and he was sentenced to six years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed. I'm also looking at the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I did that too. And I think this is the right time for the break. I do think that if I am finished today, there will not be much time left for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The next witness to be released, doesn't have to remain stand by.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will have a break, and we'll resume at ten minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just two very brief procedural matters, Your Honour. Mr. Kehoe has informed us that he will not object to the two exhibits that were MFI'd, P2556 and P2557.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, therefore, I take it that Mr. Hedaraly would not misinform the Chamber. P2556 and P2557 are admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, and the second issue was with respect to the witness discussed, Bogdan Brkic [phoen], it was a mistake in e-court that the statement was admitted under seal, there were never a protective measures motion being filed for him, so therefore I know the redaction has been made, but there is no need to redact a reference that was made. And both parties apologise for the confusion and the mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your apologies are accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, you know -- my -- I am just being showed something by Ms. Katalinic. Apparently, whether it was a mistake on our part, I think, Mr. President, the order has under seal. You admitted under seal. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll review everything in relation to this. Mr. Registrar will assist me, and we'll inform you about the results.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be resolved, and all of the information of the parties will be checked. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Mr. Perkovic, in an answer earlier today at draft transcript 64, lines 7 and 8, we were talking about being interviewed by the police, you also said: "They also brought me a paper stating that I was discharged from the Croatian military." Can you please explain to us what happened and what you were told.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I really don't know what happened. When I was being abused, they simply put a piece of paper on the table and told me, As of today, you are no longer with the armed forces. Sign it. And so I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge, the day you were arrested, you were still a member of the 15 Home Guard Regiment?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You also participated in the -- actually, let me strike that. Let me just -- one last thing. Were you told anything else about why you were signing that form?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No, they didn't say anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were you given a choice as to whether you could sign it or not?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. They just put it in front of me and said, Sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you. You also participated in the liberation of Grahovo prior to Operation Storm; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: For a month, we were deployed along the lines at the Sator mountain. We were there until Grahovo was liberated, and then we left. We were included in the operation in Grahovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So you were part of one of the units that actually took back Grahovo for the Croatian army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't advance towards Grahovo. We just spent one month prior to its liberation there, and then, on one morning, the operation took place in Grahovo, and we left the next day. But we did not go into Grahovo itself. We were replaced, and then it was that shift that moved slightly towards Grahovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about looting and burning that occurred in Grahovo after it was liberated?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't. We were not in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, during Operation Storm, your job was to mop up or clean the terrain; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: That was after Operation Storm. During Operation Storm, we had a different task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you tell us what your task was during Operation Storm?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Our task was to leave Skradin on the 4th, during the night. We had to take the villages of Ljubicici and Tepici just following the village of Laskovice. We had one group advance towards the enemy, and we, as part of the other unit, circumvented it coming from the back. We fought that whole day, and the next day around 10.00, we were replaced by other troops who penetrated the lines. By that time Knin had fallen, and then they withdrew. We went home for a few hours to wash and went back in the field. We spent the night there, and then what followed was the continuation of the operation to Kistanje. We followed the tank. We didn't take the main road, but we went another way. And passing through the villages, we saw some civilians who remained. No one touched them or anything, and when we got in Kistanje, we realized that they had just left the village, because the food on their tables was still warm.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And let me go back to the mopping up, or the terrain cleansing in which you were involved after Operation Storm. And you said earlier in answer to one of the Presiding Judge's questions, that you were not given specific instructions as to where to go. You would simply spread out and look for enemy soldiers. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Our task was to mop up the village, to see whether there are any leftover enemy soldiers or weapons. It's not that that we were allowed to with wonder about like sheep, but we were given the task of mopping up that particular village. It was in the Zrmanja area. There were several villages there, and some of our troops were sent to one village and then others to the other, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the specific instructions you were given was to go and make sure there were no enemy soldiers left behind; is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you 65 ter 7312, staying with this mopping-up issue. And this is the testimony of your platoon commander, Mr. Gojevic, during your trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If we can go to page 11 in the English. I believe it's going to be the page marked with the number -- or stamped 0874 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And there your platoon commander, Mr. Gojevic, at the top is discussing about terrain cleansing and he says: "This meant, as I understood it, to search the terrain and find the enemy's soldiers, if there were any; and before the order to go to this field trip, we were not particularly told how to deal with the civilians. We did not have any special orders regarding dealing with the civilians; but, of course, nobody told us that it is allowed to set the fires, to loot, or to kill either, as you ask. For me, personally the meaning of terrain cleansing was clear." Now, Mr. Perkovic, is it true that you were not particularly instructed as to how to deal with civilians?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Not in Zrmanja. But prior to Operation Storm, in Skradin, the chief commanding officer there did caution to us take care of civilians, so as to avoid any murders of Serb civilians. That was at the very outset of Operation Storm, and I suppose, later on, I didn't need to be told anything on top of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So the specific order that you got before Operation Storm, if I understood you correctly, was to take care of civilians so as to avoid any murders of Serb civilians. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were you given any specific caution, in terms of looting or burning houses?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't recall anyone saying anything about that. I don't think we were told that. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You mentioned Kistanje earlier on, that you arrived in Kistanje. Can you remember when you arrived Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: We arrived in Kistanje -- well, Operation Storm was launched on the 5th; that was day one. Within two days, I think. We arrived in Kistanje on the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Would it change your answer if I told that you Operation Storm was launched on the 4th of August and not the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: We had an operation on the 4th, we were replaced subsequently, we spent the night on the 5th. And the, 6th we were in Kistanje. The 4th was Operation Storm was launched. Then we went to the two villages I referred. We fought there the whole day and night, went back home for a few hours, then spent the night in the fold field. And I think on the 6th in the morning or around noon, we were in Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Is it possible that you arrived in Kistanje on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: It is not. If the operation was launched on the 4th, then the night between the 5th and 6th, we spent in the field on a meadow, and on the morning of the 6th, we went in Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show your Official Note from 16 October, D1539. And in the fifth full paragraph, you say: "The launch of Operation Storm, his unit received the task of mopping up two villages north of Rupe. They went into action during the night at around 3.00 or 4.00." So that is the night before the 4th of August. "The same day they entered the aforementioned places where they spent one day and night, until they were relieved. The next day they went into action for the liberation of Kistanje where they also sent one day and night." My question for you is: Is it possible that you're mistaken and that you were in Kistanje on the 5th of August?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No. On the 4th is when Operation Storm began. Our task was Ljubicici and Tepici. We spent the whole day and night there. The next day we went home. And on the third day, the 6th, we went to Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 4th and the 5th, it was when the Ljubicici-Tepici operation took place. We were relieved on the 5th, went home, and then went back in the field. The, next day, it was Kistanje, the 6th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you one more document, and we'll leave this topic after. If can I have 65 ter 2884. This is a report of the operation written by General Gotovina. And if we go to page 3 at the bottom. Page 2 in the B/C/S. Actually, it's page ... page 2 in the version I have. Go to page 3, please, in the English. In the B/C/S, you see in the middle, it says: "Day two of the offensive operation." You see it says: "15th DP," which is 15 Home Guard Regiment, "captured the general Kistanje area." And I don't want to insist on this, but I'll just ask you again if it is possible you were there on the 5th, and if you still believe you were there on the 6th, that's fine. But I want to show that you document to you and ask you if that changes your recollection at all.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: On the 4th we went to Ljubicici and Tepici. That was our task. We spent the whole day and the whole night there. On the 5th we were relieved to go home, spend the night in the field, when we returned. And on the 6th, we went into Kistanje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Just for clarification, if we could just turn the page and just take a look at -- I think it's on the next page, it is it not, Counsel?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It's on the screen now. The B/C/S was the right one, but now we see the English. Thank you, counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. Perkovic. Thank you for your answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: If I can tender 65 ter 2884.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: I will just take a look at it, Mr. President, We can MFI. But I don't think I have any objection, if I could just take a glance at it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It will be MFI'd for the time being.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter 2884 becomes Exhibit P2559, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Kistanje on the 6th, as you -- as you have testified that you were, did you notice any looting taking place in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: When did you see looting in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: The next day, in the morning. We were supposed to go home. A truck came by with some goods on it, and they said they were going back to Vodice. I asked if I could get a ride, since we could go home. We got up, and they stopped along the road. We went to relieve ourselves. Someone came up. There was some shouting. I asked him what it was all about, and they said that a general was there shouting at them for taking away those items, asking what kind of soldiers were they to loot. I think there was a person there, perhaps he was Krsticevic or someone else, in any case, a general came in a car that was on the main road, and he asked him why they were looting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Just to make sure that I understand, was that truck carrying goods from the houses in Kistanje, from the Serb civilian houses in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: From Kistanje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that was from Kistanje. The truck was there. I asked them if I could hitch a ride. But I don't know their names. We left Kistanje the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And did you see any HV soldiers loading up goods on that truck?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And what did -- this general, you said he was shouting at them. Did he do anything to prevent the truck from leaving?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: He shouted at them, asking what kind of soldiers they were for taking items away. They simply went on, passed by the check-points and the police, and I suppose they took that stuff home.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: So the general did not stop them from taking the property on the truck; correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: He didn't prevent them. He only shouted at them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And you said that was the day after you arrived in Kistanje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you P980, and maybe that can also help with the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: This is a statement of a witness who arrived in Kistanje 10.00 on the morning of August 6th. And he says something similar to what you have stated, so that we can get the timing right. If we go to page 8 of the statement of Mr. Dawes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Excuse me. Mr. President, he already said at the time. I mean, he is trying to change the time after the witness has given him the time. So now he has --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want to -- I don't know if we want to address it in front of the witness, but there's a -- there's a date issue, and that statement -- I have put the matter to the witness. Now that statement is going to either --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Do we have to go then, if you say there is another witness who said -- perhaps, not to put the whole of the statement. It is all about the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's about the date, and it's linked to the event that he saw, which matches what he saw. And that is in evidence, Your Honour, so I have explored the matter with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: And here is the issue. The issue is that he has been asking him about this particular date in various different forms, and he obviously doesn't like the date that's given to him. But that's the date he says. That's the bottom line.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it just about the date, or about the observations on what that witness saw and what this witness has told us? If that is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's about both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: About both. Then try to -- let's try to get it separate. If you could just for my information, without yet putting it to the witness, you said it was P8980.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: At P980 at page 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And I believe the page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. You said page -- page 8. Could you further assist us as to the paragraph. And is it page 8 in e-court, or is it -- that's the same, I see. Do you have any specific paragraph in mind, Mr. Hedaraly?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm -- my e-court seems to be -- I believe it's the second full paragraph. But I'm getting it up right now, and I'll ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I -- hardly could be the second full paragraph, which is not specific for any ... Is --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Page 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it was page 9, Mr. President. It's my mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: And the second full paragraph talks about the timing. And then the next paragraph about his observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: On page 9, second full paragraph, I have no date yet, so I'm afraid I have to go back to the next page --

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It's the bottom of the page before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We have one piece of testimony which not necessarily contradicts what this witness tells us, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily, Your Honour, but I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It can be put --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's see whether we can -- There was some discussion, Mr. Perkovic, about the day on which you arrived Kistanje. This Chamber has heard evidence on events on the 6th of August, which refers to Kistanje, and tells about looting of items, such as TV sets, stereos, small tractors. Are you certain about the date you described?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That isn't true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... it's evidence received before this Chamber. But you have a -- have you been in Kistanje the day before you said you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. We were the first to enter Kistanje on the 6th, and there was no looting or burning. Two houses may have been on fire. What was involved in was the mopping up of the village in search of enemy soldiers or weapons. And we managed to find several rifles or pistols in the village. It was only on the following morning that we were relieved, on the 7th, and were able to go home. I'm telling you that this is the way things happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As you said, you went home and got transportation from a truck which was passing. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was passing there. It had been to Kistanje and was loaded full of items.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... what time --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 7th, in the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What time, approximately, in the morning, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At around 10.00 or 11.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Can you tell us who relieved you in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I wasn't interested in knowing exactly who it was. I knew it was our army. I didn't know which particular unit. We were very tired, and we only wanted to advance in that area. I wasn't interested in those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Were you aware that a member of the 113th Brigade told this Court that by the 6th of August, 35 to 30 per cent of the town was already destroyed when he arrived in Kistanje?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: That was not the case; I'm sure of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What the witness told us, I take it, that you want to say that what this witness may have told this Court is, as far as you know, not correct. Is that what you wanted to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that many were on fire. That's for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just by way of clarity, that witness was Mr. Gojanovic that gave that testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We spent the night in Kistanje. The army was billeted in the various houses and slept there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you have answered the question. I do not know what the name of the witness adds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Yeah. I was -- I mean, I'm trying to follow the Chamber's guidance in asking the questions. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Well, I think is it certainly pertinent for the Chamber when counsel is referring to a witness who that witness was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, yes. You just wanted to assist the Chamber. That is appreciated. Please proceed, Mr. Hedaraly.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: You said not that many houses in Kistanje were destroyed. Did you go back to Kistanje after the 6th of August -- or after the 7th, when you left?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: We went along the road towards Zrmanja, which goes past the village of Kistanje, or, rather, we went through the village of Rudele which is beyond Kistanje and then on towards Zrmanja.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Did you ever see the village of Kistanje after the 7th of August?

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. And more houses were on fire than was the case on the first day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Let me show you P2349, which is a report from the Sibenik Operations Group. It's at page 6 at the bottom in the English, page 4 at the bottom in the B/C/S. And there's a statement there that I want to ask you about. And the statement says -- it should be page 6 in the English, I believe. The second item, 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Counsel, I think it's 5 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: Thank you, Counsel. My apologies. Here we go. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: It says: "The behaviour of the Croatian army when entering settled areas was correct, but when the above-mentioned settlements, in particular those with Serbian population were taken, the unit commanders lost control over their units which resulted in a large number of burned houses and many instances of looting, in particular, in the area of Djevrska, Kistanje, and Drnis." Is what is reported here consistent with your observations at the time? Yes, I'm asking if that is consistent with what you observed at the time.

utterances.speaker: PERO PERKOVIC
utterances.text: When we were at Zrmanja, and when we were going back, I only saw that there were army units which supplied food and water to the civilians in an organised manner. So I only know about Serb civilians, a lot of them elderly, who organised food supplies. So right after we went through the area, we were followed by Red Cross officials, offering food to Serb civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hedaraly, I'm looking at the clock. There may be a need for further questions, I do not know, Mr. Kehoe, whether you would need much time. There may be some questions from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Briefly, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Briefly means?

utterances.speaker: MR. KEHOE
utterances.text: Five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Five minutes. MR. Hedaraly, how much time would you still need? There may be some questions from the Bench as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HEDARALY
utterances.text: I will try to finish in the next five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
